label: February 16–22
title: “To Be a Greater Follower of Righteousness” —  Genesis 12

items.text: Abraham’s life stands as a testimony that no matter what a person’s family history has been, the future can be filled with hope. He came from a troubled family, yet his desire was 'to be a greater follower of righteousness,' and God honored that desire.
items.attribution: Come, Follow Me—For Home and Church: Old Testament 2026

items.text: Our inner desires are given life and they are seen in our choices and in our actions. God supports our righteous desires and helps us to live them out. What are your desires, and how are they evident in your actions?

God will bless us for our faith and righteous desires. Even when facing trials, like Abraham and Sarah’s unfulfilled desire for a child, the Savior helps us to embrace His promises, even if they seem to be 'afar off'.
items.attribution: Come, Follow Me—For Home and Church: Old Testament 2026

items.text: God wants us to make and keep covenants with Him, just as He made a covenant with Abraham. This covenant continues in us when we are baptized and make covenants in the temple, connecting us to His promises.
items.attribution: Come, Follow Me—For Home and Church: Old Testament 2026

items.text: God promised Abraham and his posterity blessings, including a vast posterity and an inheritance of land. As many as receive the Gospel are accounted Abraham's seed. These promises can apply to us today through our own covenants.

God not only promised blessings to Abraham but also told him, '_be_ a blessing.' This means we are to be instruments in God’s hands, sharing His love and His gospel with others, becoming a blessing to the world.

The Abrahamic covenant offers eternal parallels, fulfilling promises like an inheritance or a large posterity in the eternities. Through making and keeping covenants, we access God’s power and draw closer to Him.

We are all influenced by our families and culture, but we have a unique inner space that we control. Our desires, when given life through our choices and actions, demonstrate our commitment to righteousness and invite God’s support.

Abraham, the father of the faithful, was called the Friend of God. Despite his challenging family background, his unwavering desire for righteousness led God to honor him and establish an everlasting covenant through his lineage.

God wants us to understand the significance of His covenant with Abraham because He desires to make a similar covenant with us. By receiving His Gospel and making sacred covenants, we become part of His eternal family.
